newsitem.title: ANGOLA: UNITA changes planned Angola unity government.
newsitem.headline: UNITA changes planned Angola unity government.

text.p: Several UNITA members set to take up their places in Angola's planned unity government have been replaced, possibly delaying the establishment of the new government, UNITA and Western diplomats here said on Friday.
"Many things have changed in the past few days," said Domingos Toy, aid to chief UNITA representative in Luanda, Isaias Samakuva.
"There have been a number of changes in the people who will represent UNITA in the new government. But the reasons for these changes are for our leaders to say, not for me."
Toy said several key people to be replaced include designate Minister of Hotels and Tourism Jorge Valentim and designate Minister of Mines and Geology Kayaya Kahala.
Kahala will be replaced by Marcos Samondo, the present UNITA representative to the U.N. Security Council.
Several UNITA deputies will also be replaced, Toy said.
UNITA (the National Union for the Total Independence of Angola) and the Angolan government signed a peace agreement in the Zambian capital Lusaka in 1994.
A key provision in the agreement was the establishment of a unity government, a move seen formally ending hostilities that erupted after independence from Portugal in 1975.
But the unity government, one of the main goals of the huge U.N. mission here -- the largest in the world at over 6,000 staff -- has been repeatedly delayed.
Western diplomats here say UNITA's changes to the planned unity government have not been well received by the incumbent Angolan government.

"Several of these people being replaced are not of the stature as the ones who were meant to come," said one Western diplomat. "The government sees it as weakening the legitimacy of the unity government, reducing its importance."
Diplomats here also say the changes will undoubtedly slow the establishment of a unity government.
"All these changes have to be approved by the Supreme Court, and that will just take time," said the diplomat. "As far as I can tell this is another stalling tactic by UNITA."
UNITA's Toy says the changes should not affect the establishment of the unity government.
"As soon as the rest of the UNITA members of the government arrive we will set about setting the date for the new government," said Toy. "It shouldn't be too long now."
